Verbs + Objects + Infinitives
We use the structure verb + object + to infinitive when we want to make a request, give an advice or a warming.

There are some verbs that always require to follow the pattern following in:

Subject +verb + object + to infinitive + complement


Examples:
She advised me to review more information about UML.
They want the company to develop their software project.

Remember that the object of the sentence is the person or the thing that receives the action. In the examples above the objects are me and the company.

In the following chart, you can find some of the verbs that use this structure:
Mr. Collins wants us to make a presentation about UML. So, I advise you to be prepared.
It permits programmers to define, visualize, build, and describe software tools.

Versions of UML
UML is a standard language for modeling software systems.  It has different versions.

UML emerged the mid-1990 thanks to the development of object-oriented methods developed in the late 80's and early 90's. This modeling language integrates the notions of the Booch method, the object-modeling technique, and object-oriented software engineering.

There are two main versions of UML, 1.x and 2.x, each with multiple sub versions. In 1996, an international consortium called UML Partners proposed the first draft of this language to the OMG (Object Management Group). Then, a group of experts got together in order to define the language constructs and specifications to meet all the standardization purposes. This version, UML 1x, was finally released in November 1997.

After different versions of UML 2.X, such as UML 2.0, 2.2 and 2.4, the latest version, UML 2.5, appeared in 2015. These versions have common specifications and improvements in terms of Superstructure, Infrastructure, the Object Constraint Language, and UML Diagram Interchange.

Peter: I couldn't make it to class yesterday. Do you know if we have anything for next session?
Liz: Yes, for next class, Mr. Collins wants us to make a presentation about UML. So, I advise you to be prepared.
Peter: Really? Can you help me catch up? What do you know about UML?
Liz: Well, UML means Unified Modeling Language. It permits programmers to define, visualize, build, and describe software tools.
Peter: I see. So, UML enables users to have a standardized way to perceive the design of a system. Right?

Liz: Exactly. UML uses meta object facility and graphic notation. This is a key factor in object-oriented programming because it allows programmers to create visual models of systems.
Peter: OK. But, is UML useful during the software development cycle?
Liz: Absolutely. If you need to develop a software project, you can use UML during the whole cycle. This modeling language is able to produce entire applications. Besides, UML executables can be deployed in different types of platforms.

Peter: Wow! That seems pretty cool. And, what kind of elements does UML offer?
Liz: Well, UML includes programming language statements, actors, activities, business processes, and logical and reusable software components.
Peter: I understand. And, do all UML diagrams work the same way?
Liz: Not really. If you use UML diagrams, you need to know that they are divided into two categories. In the first type, you can find diagrams that can represent structural information. This type of diagrams allows programmers to document the architecture of software systems. The second type of diagrams represent general types of behavior, we use them to describe the functionality of systems.
